scope: Linux x64 standalone process-exit parity in the packaged and full Node, Deno, and Bun runners. Supplementary ordinary Lean comparisons and 36 unchanged upstream regressions; not full-suite or cross-platform conformance.
findings: The original adapter aliased forceExit to ordinary exit and flushed buffered stdout on forceExit in every engine. Bun full-runtime ordinary exit also lost buffered open-file data.
The private ABI now distinguishes forced termination. Standalone launchers call the same C runtime exit/_Exit functions as native Lean before JavaScript disposal can flush streams.
Normal return, ordinary exit, and forced exit now match native exit status, stdout, stderr, and the open buffered file in all three full and packaged engines.
Generated executable launchers and source launchers are checked separately. Embedded guests still throw an exit exception and leave the host process alive.
All 7267 original source hashes remain unchanged before and after each upstream registration. No upstream test or expected output was edited.
retainedDevelopmentAttempts: The first full build succeeded, but snapshot creation rejected duplicate application of a symbol-lookup optimization already supplied by the patched SDK. The unnecessary extra transform was removed; a fresh snapshot was created from the successful build. The failed preparation and partial snapshot remain retained.
remainingGaps: Embedded forced-exit disposal still closes and flushes native file streams; buffer-discard parity is unfinished.
Native macOS and Windows comparisons remain unexecuted. The Microsoft C runtime documents equivalent exit/_Exit behavior; this is a design reference, not platform validation.
Bun still uses lowered memory and the disclosed Linux stack helper.
The full suites and packaged full-runtime integration remain unfinished; no remaining gap has been established fundamental.
